- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- In periods of high volatility or sharp reversals, model fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1-2 day decay factor to recent highs/lows.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with the dominant sentiment trend; align forecast direction with the most recent sentiment majority.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 7-10 days); apply a slight upward bias to final 5-7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model may ignore underlying fundamentals; add a “sentiment-weighted” correction factor to reduce overconfidence bias.
